Results from fitted values and prediction

magCompPrediction.Rd

This help topic describes the named list with class magCompPrediction, containing requested magnitude, proportion, density, and count components, followed by metadata. Predictions made with keep_effects = TRUE also store a latent component for use by samples; its internal indexing is not part of the public interface. standSummary also returns this class, with a selected stand density, total, or proportion component. Selecting one type still returns a list: for example, fitted(fit, type = "count")$count.

Details

The definitions below describe fitted() and predict() results. See standSummary for the corresponding stand quantities and metadata.

Observed and new units each have two choices of target:

UnitsConditional meansSimulated observations
Observedfitted(target = "expected")fitted(target = "observation")
Newpredict(target = "expected")predict(target = "observation")

These calls also require the fitted object and, for prediction, newdata. Defaults are target = "expected" and summary = "mean". With both model components, type = NULL selects all four quantities. Standalone models return the quantities described below.

For fixed-area stems, let \(M\) be overall stem density, \(p_j\) the probability of final category \(j\), and \(a\) the sampling area. For each retained posterior draw, expected quantities are constructed as follows. Observation quantities additionally draw \(N \sim \mathrm{NB}(aM, r_M)\) and then \(\mathbf{Y} \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(N, \mathbf{p})\).

QuantityExpectedObservation
magnitude\(M\)\(N/a\)
proportion\(p_j\)\(Y_j/N\)
density\(M p_j\)\(Y_j/a\)
count\(a M p_j\)\(Y_j\)

In a conditional two-category model, \(p_j\) is the product of the parent probability and its conditional child probability. Size \(r_M\) uses the fitted fixed value or its matching posterior draw when estimated.

Point-sampling basal-area models support both targets. Let \(M^{BA}\) be basal-area density and \(m\) the in-tree tally. Expected total tally is \(M^{BA}/\mathrm{BAF}\). The observation target draws $$m \sim \mathrm{NB}(M^{BA}/\mathrm{BAF}, r_M^{BA}),$$ using the fitted fixed size or its matching posterior draw, then allocates \(m\) among categories when composition is fitted.

Expected magnitude and category density are \(M^{BA}\) and \(M^{BA}p_j\); observation values are the sampled basal-area estimates \(\mathrm{BAF}\,m\) and \(\mathrm{BAF}\,Y_j\). Count is the expected or simulated in-tree tally, and proportion is \(p_j\) or \(Y_j/m\), respectively. The fixed-area expressions above therefore apply with magnitude interpreted as basal-area density and exposure \(a = 1/\mathrm{BAF}\); this exposure is not a physical plot area. BAF must be constant within each point but may vary between points. BAF and basal-area density use matching units, such as square feet per acre.

For summary = "mean", each component is a matrix with one row per unit and one column per category, or one column named "total" for magnitude. For summary = "samples", category quantities have dimensions unit by category by retained sample, plus a final chain dimension for multiple chains. Magnitude omits the category dimension. For summary = "quantile", category quantities have dimensions unit by category by probability, and magnitude is a unit by probability matrix. Singleton dimensions are preserved; means and quantiles pool chains. Row and category labels identify the fitted units or prediction rows and final response cells.

Use summary(result) on a result retained with summary = "samples" to obtain a table of means, standard deviations, and quantiles by unit, quantity, and category. See summary for the returned columns. This uses the stored draws and does not rerun prediction.

For magnitude-only models, the default quantities are magnitude and count. Expected values are \(M\) and \(aM\); observation values are \(N/a\) and \(N\), with a negative-binomial draw for \(N\). The count array retains a category dimension of length one named "total". density and proportion are unavailable because no composition is fitted.

Composition-only models default to proportion. Expected probabilities need neither area nor a supplied total. Conditional expected counts are \(N p_j\); replicate counts follow \(\mathrm{Multinomial}(N,\mathbf p)\). fitted() uses observed totals; predict() requires total_count. Conditional densities divide these counts by exposure. magnitude is unavailable. Expected probabilities remain defined at zero totals, but observation proportions are NA; counts and densities are zero. A supplied total is fixed across draws, not an estimate from a separate abundance model. Nested composition retains the parent/child product.

These standalone-component rules apply to both sampling families. For point sampling, conditional densities multiply tally counts by BAF, and observation proportions are undefined when the tally is zero.

Metadata contains:

source, target, type, summary, family

The source function, target, requested quantities, summary, and response family.

units, unit_ids, exposure

Measurement units by quantity, row identifiers, and the exposures used. Exposure can be NULL for predictions requiring none.

components

Active model components.

count_conditioning

Count conditioning: "observed_total", "supplied_total", or "none". Composition-only CV identifies its assessment as conditional on observed totals.

total_count

Conditioning totals by unit when used, otherwise NULL.

n_samples, n_chains, n_draws

Retained draws per chain, number of chains, and their product.

sample_ids, chain_ids, probs

Draw positions within the original retained chain, chain labels, and requested probabilities for quantile summaries (otherwise NULL). Draws are aligned across quantities; observation simulation does not add another draw dimension. With predict(n_draws = ...), positions identify the selected subset.

proportion_conditioning

"positive_total" for observation results, otherwise "none". Observation proportions are undefined for zero totals. Their means and quantiles use positive-total draws only. Samples retain NA entries at zero totals, and all-zero units have NA proportion summaries.

zero_total_probability, n_positive_draws

For each unit, the empirical fraction of zero-total draws and number of positive-total draws across all chains. Returned for every observation result, including type subsets; NULL for expected results.

All outputs within one result use the same draws. A zero simulated total gives zero magnitude, density, and count, and undefined (NA) proportions. Relations between draw-level quantities need not hold after separately taking means or quantiles. Expected-target intervals describe uncertainty in conditional means; observation-target intervals also include variation from the likelihood.

See also

fitted, predict; the technical guide's Prediction and aggregation section in magComp-package.
